newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Grains prices ease on US crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Grains prices ease on US crop forecast.

text.p: Prospects for a big U.S. wheat crop reversed a rally in benchmark Chicago wheat futures prices on Wednesday.
In other good news for wheat buying nations, sources at the European Commission said export volumes from western Europe may also again be generous in the coming year.
On the Chicago Board of Trade soft red winter wheat for December eased some five cents per bushel in early activity to around $3.72.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture had on Tuesday pegged 1997 U.S. wheat production at 2.531 billion bushels. That figure came in above an average analyst estimate of 2.476 billion bushels.
The EU Commission sources said the European Union could export some nine million tonnes of soft wheat in the year that began on July 1.
This would not be far below the volume of around 9.8 million tonnes sold from last year's bumper harvest.
There had been talk in the trade that a rise in wheat export taxes last week signalled a clampdown on shipments.
The sources said a strong dollar, firm world prices and buoyant demand, especially from the Middle East and North Africa, created a favourable export outlook.

Plentiful supplies were expected with another huge EU grain harvest in prospect although there were fears about quality, especially of spring sown crops, following a long spell of wet weather in June and early July.
The sources also said that the wheat export tax, designed to keep a lid on internal food prices, could be slightly reduced if the dollar and U.S. grain prices shed value.
Commodity markets generally were quiet and rangebound on Wednesday.
Precious metals fluctuated around earlier intraday highs on Wednesday afternoon after the latest batch of U.S. economic data wiped away any latent inflation fears.
U.S. July retail sales rose 0.6 percent, largely matching expectations, while the U.S. July PPI fell 0.1 pct, the seventh consecutive monthly decline.
